_comment: Each entry names a security guard, a surgical edit that DISABLES it, and the
test(s) that must fail once it is disabled. The harness applies the edit, runs
the suite, asserts those named tests failed, and restores the file.
The point is the #916 lesson: a regression guard that still passes on buggy
code is worse than no guard, because it certifies the gap. A test only earns
its green when it has been seen to go red for the right reason.
Repo-level by design so any boundary can register here later (the guard trio,
secrets-guard). Registered today only for the #931 active-grant boundary — the
shape is general, the coverage is deliberately not.
Adding an entry: each edit's `find` must occur EXACTLY ONCE in `file`. Prefer disabling a
condition (`if (false && ...)`) over deleting a block, so the mutation stays
syntactically valid — a mutation that fails to COMPILE proves nothing, since
the suite would fail for the wrong reason. The harness checks the named tests

mutations.guard: index.ts property 2 — the definition is reconstructed under the authority lock and its digest compared to the displayed one
expectFailing: package bytes mutated between display and commit create no grant

mutations.guard: the in-lock digest revalidation — pre-lock reads are never trusted for the spawn decision
expectFailing: package bytes mutated INSIDE the dispatch window refuse at the in-lock match
package bytes changed after approval refuse at the digest match

mutations.guard: the verify-then-exec window is bounded to one synchronous span — no await between the in-lock digest match and process creation
expectFailing: the authority-lock callback is synchronous (an async callback would widen the window)
no await sits between the in-lock digest match and process creation
mutations._note: Two edits because an await inside a non-async arrow is a COMPILE error, and a mutation that fails to compile proves nothing — the suite would fail for the wrong reason. Made valid, this mutation changes no output: every behavioural test in the broker suite stays green and only the structural assertions in toctou.test.ts catch it. That is the case for asserting the window structurally.
